title: Path Traversal in examples/server.js via Unsanitized URL in pipeFileToResponse
analysis:
Data flow trace:
- Source: In `examples/server.js`, incoming HTTP request target `req.url` is read at line 82 from untrusted client requests.
- Sanitization/Validation: Lines 109-111 append `index.html` if the URL ends in `/`, and line 120 checks if the URL matches `/index\.html$/`. However, there is no validation or bounds checking to prevent directory traversal sequences (`../`). `path.join(__dirname, url)` resolves relative path components, allowing traversal outside the `examples` directory.
- Sink: At line 122, `pipeFileToResponse(res, url, 'text/html')` is invoked, which calls `fs.createReadStream(path.join(__dirname, file)).pipe(res)` at line 75 to read the traversed file from the filesystem and stream its content to the HTTP response.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Send an HTTP request such as:
```http
GET /../../coverage/lcov-report/index.html HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
```
or
```http
GET /../../../../../../var/www/html/ HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
```
The server will resolve the path relative to `__dirname`, traversing out of the directory and streaming the target `index.html` file back to the client.
